A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same boundary-extension framework and 18-dataset study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Poisson, elasticity, and hyperelasticity problems, including benchmark comparisons, scaling, transfer, robustness, and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds FNO experiments in Appendix F.9 and Table F.4.

M1.justification: The boundary normalization, extension strategies, and cross-attention extender remain unchanged. Appendix F.9 applies the existing learned-extension approach to FNO without introducing a new methodological component or objective.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 18 datasets and task configurations. The added FNO experiments reuse the Square Poisson datasets with Dirichlet, Mixed, and Mixed+ conditions; grid interpolation changes preprocessing, not the represented tasks.

E2.justification: Table F.4 adds FNO with zero extensions, FNO (0X), as a comparator to FNO with learned extensions, FNO (LX). The existing BENO and RIGNO/GAOT comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F.9 introduces a separate FNO protocol using uniformly interpolated fields, 4,096 training samples, 256 validation samples, and 256 test samples. Evaluation uses interpolated targets and ignores interpolation error. Existing experimental protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The architectural ablations, mesh-convergence studies, scaling and transfer analyses, noise/resolution tests, and error/attention analyses are unchanged. Appendix F.9 adds a backbone benchmark comparison rather than a distinct robustness, error, or component-ablation study.

E5.justification: Appendix F.5 and Table F.2 retain ten-seed experiments on four datasets with minimum, mean, standard deviation, and maximum reporting. The new FNO table introduces no additional repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New Table F.4 reports FNO (0X) versus FNO (LX) median relative L2 errors of 2.51% versus 1.33%, 20.0% versus 3.86%, and 30.9% versus 7.89% for Dirichlet, Mixed, and Mixed+, respectively. These are new comparisons within v2; existing results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Appendix A derivations and affinity argument, Appendix B normalization reasoning, and metric definitions remain unchanged. The new FNO discussion supplies an intuitive explanation, not additional formal theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about general boundary conditioning, unified normalization, 18 datasets, and compatibility with different neural operators. The FNO results add support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F.9 newly explains FNO's difficulty through high-frequency content introduced by zero-padding and spectral truncation, contrasting this with smoother learned extensions. It also acknowledges disregarded interpolation error. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access footnote, specifies a single CPU core for FEM, and identifies CPU versus GPU timing hardware in Table 1. Appendix F.9 documents a 0.8M-parameter FNO with depth 2, width 20, and 16 modes, plus a 0.2M-parameter extender. The hardware disclosures do not establish changed earlier runs.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained; FNO was already cited in v1. Dataset authorship and other bibliographic metadata updates, together with author-year citation formatting, do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short roadmap to Section 3 and the F.9 subsection, alongside limited wording, contact-information, and citation-style edits. Existing section order and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The single-column main text becomes a two-column conference layout with running headers and extensive figure/table reflow. Appendix G visualizations are resized and regrouped across pages. Table F.4 is added and captions are clarified, while existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: The FNO comparison adds useful evidence for compatibility with a spectral backbone, while code-access information and explicit timing hardware improve reproducibility and interpretation. The gain is limited: the new experiment uses existing interpolated datasets and ignores interpolation error, while the method, theory, and established results remain unchanged.
